concepts.title: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change

questions.a: The growing stage between childhood and adulthood (about 11-18 years) when the body and mind change fast.

questions.q: Why is adolescence called the teenage period?
questions.a: It covers ages ending in 'teen' - thirteen to nineteen - the main growth years.

questions.q: Why do adolescents need extra care and guidance?
questions.a: Rapid body and emotional changes can confuse them; support keeps them healthy and confident.

questions.q: Name two physical changes in boys at puberty.
questions.a: Voice deepening and growth of facial hair (also broader shoulders).

questions.q: Name two physical changes in girls at puberty.
questions.a: Breasts develop and hips widen (menstruation also begins).

questions.q: Why do adolescents sometimes feel moody?
questions.a: Hormone changes affect feelings; talking with family and friends helps.

questions.q: Why is hygiene extra important during adolescence?
questions.a: More sweat and oil secretions can cause odour and pimples; daily washing keeps skin healthy.

questions.q: What diet suits an adolescent best?
questions.a: A balanced diet - grains, pulses, milk, fruits, vegetables - plus plenty of water.

questions.q: Name one habit that harms adolescent health.
questions.a: Smoking, drugs or too much junk food (also staying up late).

questions.q: Which hormones cause the changes of adolescence?
questions.a: Testosterone in boys and oestrogen in girls, directed by pituitary hormones.

questions.q: Why do boys' and girls' bodies change differently?
questions.a: Their bodies release different sex hormones, which bring different changes.

questions.q: Is feeling unsure during adolescence normal? Why?
questions.a: Yes - body and feelings change fast; understanding that hormones cause it makes it easier.
